clue.text: Carriage for the French female in the money

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another means these letters go inside the money word

parts.note: la is the French feminine form of 'the'

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman with plenty of money is being shown a smart carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The French female' is not a woman at all but the French feminine article.
explanation.definitionFit: A calash is a light low-wheeled horse-drawn vehicle with a folding hood, a kind of carriage.

clue.text: Greek character set against Italian wine

parts.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek is hostile to Italian wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Chianti is a red table wine from the Tuscany region, so it is an example of an Italian vintage.

clue.text: Glare madly when alcoholic drink is served

indicators.note: doing something madly is doing it wildly and out of order

explanation.surface: Someone stares furiously when the beer arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: Lager is a light pale beer, an example of an alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Boy with an inner compulsion to become a medical practitioner

indicators.note: having something inner means it is placed inside the boy word

explanation.surface: A lad with a driving inner need to train as a doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon is a doctor who operates, one kind of qualified medical professional.

clue.text: A whale turning ocean-going craft over

indicators.note: a creature turning faces the other way, so the whale's name is read backwards

parts.note: an orc is a killer whale or grampus

explanation.surface: A whale capsizes a seagoing vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: Orc is an old word for a killer whale, a crossword favourite; reversed it gives CRO, so A + CRO + SS spells ACROSS.
explanation.definitionFit: Across and over are synonyms as prepositions, as in walking over or across a bridge to the far side.

clue.text: Mimics one in clerical dress

indicators.note: one person dressed in clothing means the letter goes inside the garment word

parts.note: copes are long cloaks worn by clergy
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An impressionist imitates a priest in vestments.
explanation.definitionFit: To copy someone is to imitate them, so copies matches mimics as a third-person verb.

clue.text: Above all, too "economical with the truth"

parts.note: over means excessively, as in overcautious
the famous civil-service euphemism for telling lies

explanation.surface: Mainly, someone is being far too sparing with the facts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Above all' looks like 'mainly' but is literal: lying above everything else.
explanation.definitionFit: Overlying describes a layer resting on top of what is beneath, positioned higher than the rest.

clue.text: Catalogue company at a disadvantage

parts.note: a set is a group of people, one's company

explanation.surface: A mail-order firm struggling against its rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catalogue company' reads as a mail-order business, but catalogue is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To set down is to record in writing, and to catalogue is to list and record items.

clue.text: The young director

parts.note: surface reading: a youthful film or theatre director
setter's reading: one who directs the young, guiding pupils in class

explanation.walkthrough: Read 'young' as a noun: the director is not young but directs the young.
explanation.definitionFit: A teacher in a school instructs and guides children, so in a sense directs young people.

clue.text: Head of family, note

explanation.surface: A memo noting who heads the family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head of family' looks like an instruction to take the first letter of family; instead 'Head' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A king is the head of state, the ruling monarch at the top of a realm.

clue.text: They receive price set in fixed arrangement

indicators.note: a fixed arrangement is letters deliberately put into a new order

explanation.surface: Customers who get goods at a price agreed in a price-fixing deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link to the indicator but is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Recipients are people who get or are given something, so the plural noun matches 'they receive'.

clue.text: Admission course

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the right to get in somewhere
second meaning: a dish served at a meal

explanation.surface: The cost of getting onto a training course.
explanation.definitionFit: An entree is both the privilege of entry to a place or society and a dish of a meal, before or as the main.

clue.text: Ignore superior air

parts.note: an air is a look or appearance

explanation.surface: Pay no attention to someone's condescending manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Superior air' reads as snootiness; split it into two words for over and look.
explanation.definitionFit: To overlook something is to fail to notice it or let it pass unremarked, which is to ignore it.

clue.text: The man's leading one at a time in a derisory way

parts.note: his means belonging to the man

explanation.surface: A man is leading people in single file while being mocked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading' tells you the man's word comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Hissing is how an audience shows scorn, so doing something hissingly is doing it with derision.

clue.text: An old sailor, a right-minded man, dancing

parts.note: an old salt is a veteran seaman
a Tory is a British Conservative, politically on the right

explanation.surface: A retired sailor and a conservative gentleman take to the dance floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'An old sailor' clues SALT alone, the 'old' coming from the phrase old salt.
explanation.definitionFit: Saltatory comes from Latin saltare, to leap, and describes leaping or relating to the art of dance.

clue.text: Bearing with average sound

indicators.note: sound means we go by how a word is pronounced rather than spelt

explanation.surface: A person whose posture is ordinary and whose judgement is sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Mien is a person's look or manner, their demeanour or carriage, just as bearing is.

clue.text: Amass support

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a post driven into the ground to hold up a structure

explanation.surface: Gather backing for a cause.
explanation.definitionFit: To pile things is to heap them up, and a pile is also a column sunk into the ground as a foundation.

clue.text: Bore down on a leading journalist

wordplay.note: a press editor, the leading journalist on a paper, read as PRESS plus ED

explanation.surface: Someone harassing a top newspaper reporter.
explanation.walkthrough: The press is journalism, and ED, the editor, leads the journalists, so 'a leading journalist' is a press ed.
explanation.definitionFit: To press is to push down on something with force, so pressed means bore down.

clue.text: Part is for Easter egg production

indicators.note: a production makes something new out of raw material, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A section of a factory is given over to making chocolate eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part' is a verb here, meaning separate.
explanation.definitionFit: To segregate is to set apart or separate, as to part one group from another.

clue.text: Favour trees to affect a transformation

indicators.note: a transformation changes the shape of things, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Someone prefers trees as a way of changing a landscape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Favour' looks like a verb but is a noun, a ribbon badge.
explanation.definitionFit: A favour is a ribbon or badge worn to show support, and a rosette is exactly such a ribbon decoration.

clue.text: Time to argue for disloyalty

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
to reason is to argue logically

explanation.surface: The moment to debate whether someone has betrayed their side.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason is betrayal of one's country or sovereign, the gravest form of disloyalty.

clue.text: Astute misrepresentation of the figure

indicators.note: misrepresenting something presents it wrongly, so the letters come out in another order

explanation.surface: A clever distortion of the numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figure' suggests a statistic; here it is a sculpted form.
explanation.definitionFit: A statue is a carved or cast figure of a person or animal.

clue.text: Academic takes exercise with daughter, the old buffoon!

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for daughter
antic is an archaic word for a clown or grotesque performer

explanation.surface: A university lecturer goes jogging with his daughter, looking a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Academic' looks like a noun for a don but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedantic and academic both describe overly scholarly, theoretical concern with fine detail and book learning.

clue.text: Tender, relatively speaking

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one who tends, a senior hospital nurse in Britain
second meaning: a family relation, a female sibling

explanation.walkthrough: 'Tender' reads as an adjective but is a noun, one who tends; in British hospitals a sister is a senior nurse in charge of a ward.
explanation.definitionFit: A sister is both a ward nurse who looks after patients and, as a relative, a daughter of the same parents.

clue.text: Hard up and so brusque

explanation.surface: Someone broke and therefore bad-tempered.
explanation.definitionFit: Short means lacking enough cash, as in short this month, and also curt or abrupt in speech.

clue.text: No smart set would make such a selection

indicators.note: to make something from these words is to build a new word out of their letters

explanation.surface: Fashionable society would never choose such a motley mix.
explanation.definitionFit: An assortment is a mixed collection of various kinds, which is a selection of things.

clue.text: Throw out some miscellaneous trinkets

indicators.note: some means only a part of the following words is taken

parts.note: sits across the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: Clearing out a few odds and ends.
explanation.definitionFit: To oust is to expel or force out, which is to throw out.

clue.text: A dramatist's jejune retreat

parts.note: a den is a private retreat

explanation.surface: A playwright's dull hideaway.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s reads as possessive but stands for 'is'. John Dryden was a 17th-century English poet and playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: Dryden wrote many Restoration plays such as All for Love, so he is an example of a dramatist.

clue.text: Not up-to-date, being retrogressive, but made progress

indicators.note: retrogressive means going backwards, so the phrase is read from its end

parts.note: new means current, up to date

explanation.surface: Something old-fashioned and backward-looking nonetheless moved forward.
explanation.walkthrough: NOT NEW written backwards gives WENT ON; the surface plays retrogressive against progress.
explanation.definitionFit: Went on is a phrasal verb meaning continued or proceeded, which is to have made progress.
